# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the
space-station chapter. Do not refuse or defer this work on the basis of an
older freeze — earlier revisions of this file carried one, and it expired.

What still applies:

- **Creative-Triad and registry gates are the remaining barrier** between a new
  chapter and the runtime. Route the work through them; do not route around.
- **Sequencing is owner-directed: do not rush to the station.** Making the
  existing story enjoyable comes first, and the need to leave must emerge from
  play rather than from a new content hook.
- **The demo's release surface is unchanged** — it still stops at
  `ch4-arrival`, and publishing remains a separate decision. Building past it
  is allowed; shipping it in the demo is not implied.
- **Shipped copy and audio remain protected baselines.** Changing a protected
  audio/runtime path is still a contracted change, not an incidental one.
- **"Anchorage" is retired as a name.** The location is the **space station**.

# Common Ground — implementation interface plan (ch13)

Preparation only, 2026-09-06. No runtime/main source edit, no build, test, probe or signature was performed. Symbols below were read from the live worktree (including untracked `beats/` and `autopilot/`), not from the older survey. Geometry numbers (selected instrument range, socket assignment, arena coordinates, exact sample/route layout) are **deferred input** from the signed scene contract; nothing here selects them. This plan assumes the accepted direction only and proposes no creative content.

## 0. Rules for the one integration engineer

Namespaced chapter-local modules; each shared file receives a **single small call**, no refactor of `storyState.ts`, `emergentStoryDirector.ts`, `storyDirector.ts`, `App.tsx`, `EfficientScene.tsx`, `EfficientPlayer.tsx`. All of those are dirty; re-check `ls -l` immediately before edit and never reset/stash. Score uses the existing `storyScore.ts` facade only — no engine graph, no new instrument, no bundle.

## 1. New chapter-local files (all new; no existing file moves)

| File | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `story/commonGroundState.ts` | Versioned bounded trace state, reducers, serialize/hydrate/migrate/reset. Pure; no React or world imports. |
| `story/commonGroundRoute.ts` | Prop/solid-aware grounded route validation and walked-prefix predicate. Pure over injected terrain/solid queries. |
| `story/commonGroundDirector.ts` | Enter/tick dispatch, objective facts, commit events, marker target, interaction registration. |
| `story/commonGroundScore.ts` | ch13 mood/variant table + live-only coda, via `storyScore` APIs. |
| `story/commonGroundActor.ts` | The single ch13 writer of W-7744's pose + presence branch. |
| `story/world/CommonGroundWorld.tsx` | Trace render, fixed plate, world-handle registration, save restore/clear boundary. |
| `story/beats/ch13/{ch13-home,ch13-return,ch13-survey,ch13-common}.ts` | Four `defineBeat` contracts; filename === beat id. |
| `story/beats/ch13/{index.ts,definitions.ts}` | **`index.ts` must exist before the first generator run** (`emit` reads before write). |
| `story/autopilot/rail-ch13-*.ts` | Rails; move/look/act only. |
| colocated `*.test.ts` | See §9. |

## 2. Finite bounded trace state — `commonGroundState.ts`

Exported surface (proposed, exact):

```ts
export const COMMON_GROUND_SNAPSHOT_VERSION = 1;
export interface TraceSample { x: number; y: number; z: number; corner: boolean }
export interface TraceSlot {
  id: 'accepted' | 'working';
  samples: readonly TraceSample[];  // <= MAX_SAMPLES
  lengthUnits: number;              // <= MAX_TRACE_UNITS
  testedPrefixCount: number;        // samples proven by an actual test
  tailRevision: number;             // monotonic; bumps only on tail edit
  offeredEndIndex: number | null;
}
export interface CommonGroundSnapshot {
  version: typeof COMMON_GROUND_SNAPSHOT_VERSION;
  actorId: string; worldId: string;
  slots: Readonly<Record<'accepted' | 'working', TraceSlot | null>>;
  witness: { index: number; offered: boolean } | null;   // at most one
  reciprocal: { held: boolean } | null;
  hold: { reason: 'out-of-range' | 'unsupported' | 'occluded' | null };
  safePose: TraceSample | null;
}
createEmptySnapshot(actorId, worldId)
appendSample(s, sample)          // honest stop at capacity
reviseTail(s, fromIndex)         // preserves testedPrefixCount, bumps tailRevision
invalidateTestedPrefix(s, from)  // only on real voxel/support change
clearUncommitted(s)              // explicit proposal reset only
serializeCommonGround(s) / hydrateCommonGround(raw, actorId, worldId)
migrateCommonGround(raw)         // absent/legacy -> null, never throws
```

Invariants tests must pin: capacity stop never decimates a recorded corner; `reviseTail` never lowers `testedPrefixCount`; wrong `actorId`/`worldId` hydrates to `null`, not a partial graft; `clearUncommitted` never touches `accepted`; pause / failed input / Continue never call it.

**Numeric constants (`MAX_SAMPLES`, `MAX_TRACE_UNITS`, spacing, corner threshold, witness radii/tolerances, selected instrument range, socket heights) are declared as named exports with no committed values in this plan.** They are contract-supplied.

## 3. Persistence seam — `main/src/game/systems/persistence.ts`

Copy the `WorldSave.habitat` precedent exactly (`persistence.ts:239` interface, `:253` snapshot, `:301` restore): add `commonGround?: unknown` to `WorldSave`, write it in `saveWorld` beside `habitat` guarded by `worldId`, add `restoreCommonGroundForWorld` / `clearCommonGroundForWorld` alongside `restoreHabitatForWorld`, and have `clearWorldStateForWorld` clear it for **that world only**. No `GlobalSave` change. Ledgers (`observationLedger`, `accomplishmentLedger`) stay optional evidence and must not gate progression. `restartStory()` (`storyState.ts:775`) needs an explicit ch13 clear call; it does not clear ledgers today.

## 4. Actor: single pose writer, prop-aware grounded route

`AuditWorker.tsx` renders `getAuditWorkerPose()` — keep it the only body; `commonGroundActor.ts` is the sole writer while a ch13 beat is active (`A4WorldChoreography` writes only during `a4-exhale`; no overlap). `auditWorkerPresence.ts::shouldMountAuditWorker` (`:11`, sole export) needs one explicit ch13 branch independent of `FIELD_PACK_DROPPED_MILESTONE`; A4's pack/absence proof stays green. Routing reuses unmodified: `agentSurfaceNavigationRuntime.ts::createLiveAgentSurfaceTerrain` (`:13`), `agentSurfaceNavigation.ts::planAgentSurfaceRoute` (`:305`, with `AgentSurfaceRouteOptions` / `AgentSurfaceRouteReason` / `AgentSurfaceRoute`), `groundedSurfaceMotion.ts::{groundedSurfaceRouteLength, sampleGroundedSurfaceRoute, turnGroundedHeadingToward}`.

**Known gap (pass 2):** the voxel planner does not know the real trunk collider and can plan through it. The correction is a solid-occluder guard in `commonGroundRoute.ts` layered over `planAgentSurfaceRoute` — not in the shared navigation module, not in worldgen. Unreachable / unsupported / out-of-range return distinct typed reasons and hold at the last safe sample; never a teleport or timer-derived success.

## 5. Dormant reactivation and live dispatch (four one-line seams)

1. `StoryDirectorDriver.tsx` — beside the `!story.active` branch that calls `tickChapter10FreePlayEntry` (`:181`) and publishes `stationReturnObjective` (`:146`), one bounded `tickCommonGroundEntry(...)`. It must use `reactivateStoryAtBeat('ch13-home')` (`storyState.ts:821`), never `advanceToBeat` (`:808`, leaves `active:false`).
2. `emergentStoryDirector.ts` — one ch13 dispatch line each in `enterEmergentStoryBeat` (`:645`) and `emergentStoryDirectorTick` (`:787`), preserving guidance-clear + signed-AV-enter semantics and the `syncEmergentObjectiveGuidance` publication gate.
3. `storyState.ts` — ch13 resume clauses in `storyEntryPoint()` (`:246`) **before** the `ch10Complete` clause, returning `alive` explicitly (else falls through to `bare`); four ids added to `STORY_BEAT_ORDER` (`:333`) before `done`; `StoryChapter`/`StoryBeat` unions and `STORY_MILESTONES` (`:120`) gain ch13 rows. `done` stays last.
4. `beats/index.ts` — add the `ch13` import (the generator does not).

Objective facts: extend `objectivePrimitives.ts::StoryObjectiveGuidanceFacts` (`:84`) with a compact ch13 block plus defaults in `DEFAULT_STORY_OBJECTIVE_GUIDANCE_FACTS` (`:116`); ch13 prose/resolvers live in `beats/ch13/`. Marker: extend `worldHandles.ts::WorldMarkerHandle` (`:9`), resolve via `markerTargets.ts::resolveMarkerTarget` (`:20`), call `registerStoryMarkerWorld` (`:10`) from `CommonGroundWorld.tsx` — one marker authority, no new overlay. Interaction: add ids to `interactionSystem.ts::InteractionId` (`:9`, must match `story-${string}`), extend the exhaustive policy in `storyInteractions.ts`, register one world-scoped resolver via `registerStoryInteraction` (`:287`) with explicit priority/class/owner and cleanup. No player-loop or key change; build mode keeps F.

## 6. Registered ch13 beats and the strict EXTERNAL boundary

Four contracts via `beats/beatContract.ts::defineBeat` (`:73`); `entry: 'reactivation-from-done'` for `ch13-home`, `'sequence'` for the rest; every `rail` declares `stuckAfterSeconds` and `waitReason` and may not grant/mark/advance.

`chapter-registry.json` (`main/chapter-registry.json`, keys `schema | runtimeAuthorityRef | terminalBeat | sceneContracts | chapters`) gets a `ch13` record with `order: 11` (array position, not chapter number), `beats`, `before: ['ch10']`, `entry`, `exit`, `checkpoints`, `objectiveRefs`, `revealRefs`, and a new `sceneContracts` entry.

`tools/chapter-registry-gate.mjs::validateAdjacency` requires exact predecessor-exit / next-entry `stateRefs` equality. Ch10's real exit is `state:control/flight` + `state:space-station/targeted` + `state:station/docking-authorized`; ch13's real entry is restored hearth, on-foot Origin, station departed. **Do not add false guarantees to ch10 and do not drop true ch13 entry requirements.** Add a named `externalTransitions` record to the registry, its schema and the gate:

```
{ id: 'ch10->ch13-via-station',
  from: {chapter:'ch10', exitBeat:'ch10-transit'},
  to:   {chapter:'ch13', entryBeat:'ch13-home'},
  hostSegments: ['station(ch11)','return(ch12)'],
  producedReceipts: [ the four ch11/ch12 receipt strings ],
  entryGuarantees: [...], evidenceRefs: [...] }
```

Ordinary adjacency stays strict and unchanged; the transition proves both boundaries independently. Receipt strings stay byte-identical, owned by `spaceStationStory.ts::STATION_STORY_MILESTONES` (`:29`; `bootstrapStationStorySession :108`, `deriveStationStoryStep :134`, `issueBondedCell :179`, `commitStationDeparted :201`) and `stationReturnStory.ts::STATION_RETURN_MILESTONES` (`:16`; `installTidegardenBondedCell :109`, `stationReturnPending :39`, `stationReturnObjective :56`, `stationReturnMarkerTarget :85`, `STATION_RETURN_INSTALL_REACH :137`). Do not reimplement either transaction.

New `state:` refs need a producer in `storyBoundaryTelemetry.ts` (`deriveStoryBoundaryState :120`, `readStoryBoundaryRuntime :208`, `publishStoryBoundaryTelemetry :264`) **before** the allowlist `SUPPORTED_STATE_REF_PATTERNS` (`chapter-registry-gate.mjs:27`) gains a pattern. `story-authority.json` (`runtimeBeatOrder`, `runtimeEvidenceChain`, `activeProduction`, `openReleaseGates`) and `chapter-journey-contract.json` change only after signature; the `ch4-arrival` demo ceiling is untouched.

Generator order: create `beats/ch13/index.ts` → `npm run chapter:registry:generate` → hand-add the `ch13` registry record and the `beats/index.ts` import → `chapter:registry:check`, `chapter:journey:check`.

## 7. Rail seams: station movie → depart → flight → Tidegarden → install → next chapter

Pinned: `App.enterSpaceStation` strips `story`, `movie` and debug flags before the hard navigation — **a rehearsal `story=<beat>` must never be reintroduced or the completed save is reseeded**. `SpaceStationSandbox.onSequenceComplete` persists departure and returns with `undock`/`fly`, consumed by `spaceStationUndock.ts::{parseUndockFlag :22, requestedUndockAddress :39, searchAfterUndockConsumed :49, undockedShipPose :66}`. `StationScreeningDriver.tsx` currently ends after cell acquisition + dwell.

Required seam chain, each phase bounded and reporting `stuck` rather than rescuing: `stationmovie=1` → real airlock/depart action → screening-intent carried on the return URL **without** `story=` → `undock`/`fly` reconstruction → flight/landing rail → real `installTidegardenBondedCell` F action in `world/TidegardenSettlementWorld.tsx` → invitation at the certified-home core → ch13 entry watch. `autopilot/primitives.ts::isMovieStationBridgeActive` (`:1732`) stays eligible whenever ch10 is complete today; it must yield once departure/return supersedes it. Rails derive from `autopilot/rails.ts::BEAT_RAILS` (`:5`); `railDiscipline.test.ts` pins a 29-file census — update it honestly.

## 8. Score and signed AV

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
# Continuation acceptance requirements

These are verification obligations for the commissioned continuation, not new canon or a signed scene treatment.

1. An existing save with the second hearth restored reaches the next authored action without replaying cell issuance, consuming another cell, losing the home, or restarting an earlier chapter. Saves before that point retain their actual progress.
2. The station visit and return have explicit, truthful transition ownership. The chapter registry must not claim that arrival at the station already guarantees restoration at Tidegarden. Preserve the established ch11/ch12 receipts.
3. The movie path carries the real issued cell out of the station, returns physically, restores the hearth, and enters the continuation through the same completion predicates as manual play. Diagnostic preparation is marked and cannot masquerade as continuity. No timeout rescue counts as passing.
4. The new mechanic changes through meaningful physical actions. A caption, marker, dwell timer, or musical cue alone cannot commit success. Invalid actions produce useful, specific feedback; corrections are reversible and do not require repeating a collection quota.
5. Durable progression uses the established typed/versioned authority. Observations remain non-gating; presentation and score are never progression authorities. Interrupted or repeated transactions are idempotent.
6. Every guided non-cinematic state has an actionable standing work order, the exact corresponding marker, reachable target, and one semantic entry/progress/completion response. Objectives clear or replace correctly after completion, retreat, reload, deep link, pause/focus, quit, and replay.
7. Manual and movie routes preserve agency in the same places. W-7744's independent decision is legible as his decision within the approved character direction; the movie cannot inject an otherwise unreachable receipt or move him across an invalid leg.
8. The scene remains at the approved reality ceiling. Required meaning survives reduced motion, mobile controls and the lowest supported graphics tier. No key observation depends solely on colour, a musical cue, a post effect, or an unlabelled offscreen target.
9. Chapter-local rendering/audio state is inert outside the chapter and clears on all exits. Reuse the existing camera, material, lighting, score and HUD authorities. Interaction must not trigger shader/light-topology churn or a duplicate audio graph.
10. Record exact pre-change source and build identity, preserve unrelated concurrent changes, and verify the actual owned Paravoxia preview. Port liveness alone is insufficient. Serialize hardware work with the shared heavy-job lock.
11. Required proof includes relevant pure state/transition and regression tests, registry and story authority gates, full repository verification, three cold journeys without timeout rescues, supported input and reset variants, current headed hardware frames and audio, and fresh independent narrative/score/cinema/player-experience/cohesion review bound to the final contract.

Standing owner approval is recorded separately. It permits in-scope decisions; it does not convert missing evidence into a pass.

content.content:
collector.assert(manifest.schema === 'paravoxia.storyAuthority.v2', 'manifest.schema', 'Story authority manifest schema must be paravoxia.storyAuthority.v2')
  collector.assert(manifest.status?.documentationLane === 'existing-story-reconciliation', 'manifest.docs-lane', 'Documentation lane must identify existing-story reconciliation')
  collector.assert(manifest.status?.runtimeLane === 'owner-authorized-implemented-release-gated', 'manifest.runtime-lane', 'Runtime lane must distinguish implemented Story from release approval')
  // The ceiling is DATA, not a literal. Freezing which beat it names meant an
  // authorized run could not raise it without editing its own gate; the
  // invariant worth keeping is that the manifest names a real implemented beat,
  // and `manifest.runtime-ceiling-order` below still pins it immediately before
  // the terminal, so the ceiling can only ever be the last implemented beat.
  collector.assert(
    nonEmptyString(manifest.status?.runtimeStoryCeiling)
      && (manifest.runtimeBeatOrder || []).includes(manifest.status.runtimeStoryCeiling),
    'manifest.runtime-ceiling',
    'Implemented runtime ceiling must name a beat the runtime actually implements'
  )
  collector.assert(manifest.status?.releaseStoryCeiling === 'ch4-arrival', 'manifest.release-ceiling', 'Unpublished implementation must preserve the current release ceiling')
  collector.assert(manifest.status?.runtimeTerminalBeat === 'done', 'manifest.runtime-terminal', 'The runtime terminal must remain done')
  collector.assert(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(manifest.snapshotDate || ''), 'manifest.snapshot-date', 'Story authority snapshotDate must be an ISO calendar date')

  const authoritySchema = readJson(
    path.join(repoRoot, 'docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/schemas/paravoxia-story-authority.schema.json'),
    collector,
    'manifest.schema-read'
  )
  const schemaConstFields = [
    'schema',
    'status',
    'sources',
    'dynamicSources',
    'sourcePrecedence',
    'activeProduction',
    'runtimeBeatOrder',
    'runtimeEvidenceChain',
    'openReleaseGates',
    'lockedOpenQuestions',
    'requiredCouncilRoles',
    'requiredIndependentReviews'
  ]
  for (const field of schemaConstFields) {
    collector.assert(
      JSON.stringify(authoritySchema?.properties?.[field]?.const) === JSON.stringify(manifest[field]),
      'manifest.schema-const',
      `JSON Schema const for ${field} must exactly match the live story-authority manifest`
    )
  }
  collector.assert(
    JSON.stringify(authoritySchema?.required) === JSON.stringify(Object.keys(manifest)),
    'manifest.schema-required',
    'JSON Schema required fields must exactly cover the story-authority manifest'
  )

  const expectedPrecedence = [
    'runtimeBeatAuthority',
    'releaseAuthority',
    'canon',
    'ownerApprovedSceneContract',
    'executionPlan',
    'designLineage'
  ]
  collector.assert(JSON.stringify(manifest.sourcePrecedence) === JSON.stringify(expectedPrecedence), 'manifest.source-precedence', 'Story authority precedence must preserve runtime, release, canon, approved-contract, execution, then lineage order', {
    expected: expectedPrecedence,
    actual: manifest.sourcePrecedence
  })
  const sceneContractSource = manifest.dynamicSources?.ownerApprovedSceneContract
  collector.assert(
    sceneContractSource?.kind === 'run-artifact'
      && sceneContractSource?.schema === 'paravoxia.sceneContract.v1'
      && sceneContractSource?.pathPattern === '.codex/production-runs/<run-id>/scene-contract.json'
      && sceneContractSource?.activePath === '../.codex/production-runs/2026-07-13-distance-between-fires/scene-contract.json'
      && sceneContractSource?.authorityCondition === 'matching-production-lock-and-explicit-owner-approval',
    'manifest.dynamic-scene-contract',
    'ownerApprovedSceneContract must be a declared, run-scoped source gated by the matching production lock and explicit owner approval'
  )
  const declaredSourceClasses = new Set([
    ...Object.keys(manifest.sources || {}),
    ...Object.keys(manifest.dynamicSources || {})
  ])
  for (const sourceClass of manifest.sourcePrecedence || []) {
    collector.assert(declaredSourceClasses.has(sourceClass), 'manifest.precedence-source', `Source precedence references undeclared source class ${sourceClass}`)
  }

  const sourceEntries = [
    manifest.sources?.runtimeBeatAuthority,
    ...(manifest.sources?.runtimeEvidence || []),
    manifest.sources?.shippedOverview,
    manifest.sources?.canon,
    manifest.sources?.executionPlan,
    manifest.sources?.releaseAuthority,
    manifest.sources?.creativeCouncil,
    ...(manifest.sources?.designLineage || [])
  ]
  for (const source of sourceEntries) {
    const resolved = typeof source === 'string' ? path.resolve(mainRoot, source) : ''
    collector.assert(Boolean(source) && resolved.startsWith(`${repoRoot}${path.sep}`) && fs.existsSync(resolved), 'manifest.source', `Authority source must resolve inside the repository: ${source}`)
  }

  const storyState = readText(path.resolve(mainRoot, manifest.sources.runtimeBeatAuthority), collector, 'runtime.read')
  const runtimeBeats = extractBeatOrder(storyState, collector)
  const manifestBeats = manifest.runtimeBeatOrder || []
  collector.assert(JSON.stringify(runtimeBeats) === JSON.stringify(manifestBeats), 'runtime.beat-order', 'Machine authority must exactly match the implemented STORY_BEAT_ORDER', { runtimeBeats, manifestBeats })
  collector.assert(new Set(manifestBeats).size === manifestBeats.length, 'manifest.beat-duplicates', 'Runtime beat order cannot contain duplicate IDs')
  const runtimeCeilingIndex = manifestBeats.indexOf(manifest.status?.runtimeStoryCeiling)
  collector.assert(
    runtimeCeilingIndex >= 0 && manifestBeats[runtimeCeilingIndex + 1] === manifest.status?.runtimeTerminalBeat,
    'manifest.runtime-ceiling-order',
    'The runtime terminal must immediately follow the implemented Story ceiling'
  )
  const releaseCeilingIndex = manifestBeats.indexOf(manifest.status?.releaseStoryCeiling)
  collector.assert(
    releaseCeilingIndex >= 0 && releaseCeilingIndex < runtimeCeilingIndex,
    'manifest.release-before-runtime',
    'Release ceiling must remain earlier than the owner-authorized implementation ceiling'
  )

  const expectedActiveProduction = {
    runId: '2026-07-13-distance-between-fires',
    sceneId: 'distance-between-fires',
    contractVersion: 'intent-v1',
    productionLockPath: '../.codex/production-runs/2026-07-13-distance-between-fires/production-lock.json',
    implementationStatus: 'runtime-implemented',
    releaseStatus: 'gated-unpublished'
  }
  collector.assert(
    JSON.stringify(manifest.activeProduction) === JSON.stringify(expectedActiveProduction),
    'manifest.active-production',
    'Active production identity and implemented-but-unpublished status are protected',
    { expected: expectedActiveProduction, actual: manifest.activeProduction }
  )

  const activeContractPath = typeof sceneContractSource?.activePath === 'string'
    ? path.resolve(mainRoot, sceneContractSource.activePath)
    : ''
  collector.assert(
    Boolean(activeContractPath) && activeContractPath.startsWith(`${repoRoot}${path.sep}`) && fs.existsSync(activeContractPath),
    'production.contract-path',
    'Active scene contract must resolve inside the repository'
  )
  const sceneContract = activeContractPath
    ? readJson(activeContractPath, collector, 'production.contract-read')
    : null
  const productionLockPath = typeof manifest.activeProduction?.productionLockPath === 'string'
    ? path.resolve(mainRoot, manifest.activeProduction.productionLockPath)
    : ''
  collector.assert(
    Boolean(productionLockPath) && productionLockPath.startsWith(`${repoRoot}${path.sep}`) && fs.existsSync(productionLockPath),
    'production.lock-path',
    'Active production lock must resolve inside the repository'
  )
  const productionLock = productionLockPath
    ? readJson(productionLockPath, collector, 'production.lock-read')
    : null
  collector.assert(
    sceneContract?.schema === 'paravoxia.sceneContract.v1'
      && sceneContract?.sceneId === manifest.activeProduction?.sceneId
      && sceneContract?.contractVersion === manifest.activeProduction?.contractVersion
      && sceneContract?.status === 'frozen',
    'production.contract-identity',
    'Machine authority must point at the exact frozen scene contract identity'
  )
  collector.assert(
    JSON.stringify(sceneContract?.scope?.beats) === JSON.stringify(EXPECTED_PRODUCTION_BEATS),
    'production.contract-beats',
    'Frozen scene-contract beat order must match the implemented continuation',
    { expected: EXPECTED_PRODUCTION_BEATS, actual: sceneContract?.scope?.beats }
  )
  collector.assert(
    productionLock?.schema === 'paravoxia.productionLock.v1'
      && productionLock?.runId === manifest.activeProduction?.runId
      && productionLock?.status === 'locked'
      && productionLock?.currentRestrictions?.postArrivalStoryMutationAllowed === true
      && productionLock?.currentRestrictions?.copyChangeDecisionRefs?.includes('owner-instruction-2026-07-13-implement-all')
      && productionLock?.publishAllowed === false
      && productionLock?.releaseCandidate === false,
    'production.lock-authority',
    'Production lock must authorize implementation while forbidding publication and release-candidate claims'
  )
  collector.assert(
    JSON.stringify(productionLock?.lockedBeats) === JSON.stringify(EXPECTED_PRODUCTION_BEATS),
    'production.locked-beats',
    'Production lock and frozen scene contract must protect the same beat order'
  )

  for (const sourceClass of manifest.sourcePrecedence || []) {
    collector.assert(declaredSourceClasses.has(sourceClass), 'manifest.precedence-source', `Source precedence references undeclared source class ${sourceClass}`)
  }

  const sourceEntries = [
    manifest.sources?.runtimeBeatAuthority,
    ...(manifest.sources?.runtimeEvidence || []),
    manifest.sources?.shippedOverview,
    manifest.sources?.canon,
    manifest.sources?.executionPlan,
    manifest.sources?.releaseAuthority,
    manifest.sources?.creativeCouncil,
    ...(manifest.sources?.designLineage || [])
  ]
  for (const source of sourceEntries) {
    const resolved = typeof source === 'string' ? path.resolve(mainRoot, source) : ''
    collector.assert(Boolean(source) && resolved.startsWith(`${repoRoot}${path.sep}`) && fs.existsSync(resolved), 'manifest.source', `Authority source must resolve inside the repository: ${source}`)
  }

  const storyState = readText(path.resolve(mainRoot, manifest.sources.runtimeBeatAuthority), collector, 'runtime.read')
  const runtimeBeats = extractBeatOrder(storyState, collector)
  const manifestBeats = manifest.runtimeBeatOrder || []
  collector.assert(JSON.stringify(runtimeBeats) === JSON.stringify(manifestBeats), 'runtime.beat-order', 'Machine authority must exactly match the implemented STORY_BEAT_ORDER', { runtimeBeats, manifestBeats })
  collector.assert(new Set(manifestBeats).size === manifestBeats.length, 'manifest.beat-duplicates', 'Runtime beat order cannot contain duplicate IDs')
  const runtimeCeilingIndex = manifestBeats.indexOf(manifest.status?.runtimeStoryCeiling)
  collector.assert(
    runtimeCeilingIndex >= 0 && manifestBeats[runtimeCeilingIndex + 1] === manifest.status?.runtimeTerminalBeat,
    'manifest.runtime-ceiling-order',
    'The runtime terminal must immediately follow the implemented Story ceiling'
  )
  const releaseCeilingIndex = manifestBeats.indexOf(manifest.status?.releaseStoryCeiling)
  collector.assert(
    releaseCeilingIndex >= 0 && releaseCeilingIndex < runtimeCeilingIndex,
    'manifest.release-before-runtime',
    'Release ceiling must remain earlier than the owner-authorized implementation ceiling'
  )

  const expectedActiveProduction = {
    runId: '2026-07-13-distance-between-fires',
    sceneId: 'distance-between-fires',
    contractVersion: 'intent-v1',
    productionLockPath: '../.codex/production-runs/2026-07-13-distance-between-fires/production-lock.json',
    implementationStatus: 'runtime-implemented',
    releaseStatus: 'gated-unpublished'
  }
  collector.assert(
    JSON.stringify(manifest.activeProduction) === JSON.stringify(expectedActiveProduction),
    'manifest.active-production',
    'Active production identity and implemented-but-unpublished status are protected',
    { expected: expectedActiveProduction, actual: manifest.activeProduction }
  )

  const activeContractPath = typeof sceneContractSource?.activePath === 'string'
    ? path.resolve(mainRoot, sceneContractSource.activePath)
    : ''
  collector.assert(
    Boolean(activeContractPath) && activeContractPath.startsWith(`${repoRoot}${path.sep}`) && fs.existsSync(activeContractPath),
    'production.contract-path',
    'Active scene contract must resolve inside the repository'
  )
  const sceneContract = activeContractPath
    ? readJson(activeContractPath, collector, 'production.contract-read')
    : null
  const productionLockPath = typeof manifest.activeProduction?.productionLockPath === 'string'
    ? path.resolve(mainRoot, manifest.activeProduction.productionLockPath)
    : ''
  collector.assert(
    Boolean(productionLockPath) && productionLockPath.startsWith(`${repoRoot}${path.sep}`) && fs.existsSync(productionLockPath),
    'production.lock-path',
    'Active production lock must resolve inside the repository'
  )
  const productionLock = productionLockPath
    ? readJson(productionLockPath, collector, 'production.lock-read')
    : null
  collector.assert(
    sceneContract?.schema === 'paravoxia.sceneContract.v1'
      && sceneContract?.sceneId === manifest.activeProduction?.sceneId
      && sceneContract?.contractVersion === manifest.activeProduction?.contractVersion
      && sceneContract?.status === 'frozen',
    'production.contract-identity',
    'Machine authority must point at the exact frozen scene contract identity'
  )
  collector.assert(
    JSON.stringify(sceneContract?.scope?.beats) === JSON.stringify(EXPECTED_PRODUCTION_BEATS),
    'production.contract-beats',
    'Frozen scene-contract beat order must match the implemented continuation',
    { expected: EXPECTED_PRODUCTION_BEATS, actual: sceneContract?.scope?.beats }
  )
  collector.assert(
    productionLock?.schema === 'paravoxia.productionLock.v1'
      && productionLock?.runId === manifest.activeProduction?.runId
      && productionLock?.status === 'locked'
      && productionLock?.currentRestrictions?.postArrivalStoryMutationAllowed === true
      && productionLock?.currentRestrictions?.copyChangeDecisionRefs?.includes('owner-instruction-2026-07-13-implement-all')
      && productionLock?.publishAllowed === false
      && productionLock?.releaseCandidate === false,
    'production.lock-authority',
    'Production lock must authorize implementation while forbidding publication and release-candidate claims'
  )
  collector.assert(
    JSON.stringify(productionLock?.lockedBeats) === JSON.stringify(EXPECTED_PRODUCTION_BEATS),
    'production.locked-beats',
    'Production lock and frozen scene contract must protect the same beat order'
  )

/**
 * The apparatus's fixed reference socket: base + 1.30, lying exactly ON the
 * cap's top face at (-34, 52.35, 20).
 *
 * WRITTEN AS THE QUALIFIED LITERAL, NOT AS `51.05 + 1.3`. In binary that sum is
 * 52.349999999999994 — six femtometres BELOW the cap's top plane, which puts the
 * socket inside its own housing and makes every reference ray an interior
 * crossing. The instrument then occludes itself from everywhere and no route can
 * ever be demonstrated. The contact rule is deliberately epsilon-free (a
 * 0.12-thick slab must still block), so the fix belongs here, in the coordinate,
 * exactly as the qualification states it.
 */
export const CG_FIXED_SOCKET: CommonGroundPoint = Object.freeze({ x: -34, y: 52.35, z: 20 });

/** The nominal socket height the literal above realizes; asserted by the tests. */
export const CG_FIXED_SOCKET_NOMINAL_HEIGHT = FIXED_REFERENCE_SOCKET_HEIGHT;

# Producer integration inbox

No new task beyond the signed contract. Do not begin before contract-gate-pass.json is exact and passed. Preserve frozen bytes and all existing dirty source.

## Initial approach versus a revised suffix

The exact signed Cinema qualification is binding: route-offered's W-to-S language describes the first survey approach. A reoffered edited suffix resumes from the actor's actual last tested point and preserves earned prefix and pose. Never manufacture a return to inspection W or replay the initial approach. See cinema-signature-notes.md. Revision-ready is pre-F readiness for the existing voluntary branch, not a new physical verb; real tail-reopened F then starts quiet suffix drawing toward E, and the old revision marker/F prompt clears.

## Phase 1 producer spot check — concrete state-module fixes before callers depend on it

The first `commonGroundState.ts` is present; these are actual source findings, not a new design request:

1. The snapshot currently has only `survey.slot`. The signed two-slot design needs an independently retained accepted route plus a working/alternate route, including their earned classes. A new optional proposal/reset must not erase the accepted route. Keep total storage bounded to two slots; don't quietly replace the accepted proof with the next proposal. Adapt the current interface now before shared callers grow around the one-slot shape.
2. `hydrateCommonGround` currently accepts inconsistent data: it substitutes `{}` for missing structures, clamps/falls back on malformed fields, and accepts `common.committed=true` with no valid route, `terraUnits=0`, or inconsistent stage/proof/final-offer flags. It can also retain out-of-range indices/units and a routeClass without a completed tested route. This contradicts the strict consistency requirement already in the commission and trace-candidate producer review. Reject malformed/inconsistent snapshots as null; preserve valid earned facts while clearing only live occupancy. Add adversarial payload tests for actual impossible tuples, not merely wrong identity/version. No fake completion from either hydration or a presentation-only flag.
3. `TraceSlot.lengthUnits` and hydration currently use only distances between sampled points. The 120-unit cap applies to actual walked distance, including unsampled movement; a curve/loop between nominal samples cannot become free distance. Carry the actual accumulated distance and validate it consistently, with real segment support/solid checks in the live sampler. `reviseTail` must preserve the tested portion's real walked length, and pause/resume cannot reset pending movement debt. A no-op edit should not change downstream revision identity.

Continue implementing; these are in the existing signed state/route scope. Root has not edited your runtime source.

## Phase 1 route spot check — actual endpoint shortcut and socket mismatch

4. `routeProgressUnits` currently scans every polyline segment and accepts the furthest projection. `routeProgressUnits(CG_ROUTE_COMMON, CG_POSES.C, 0)` therefore returns all 18 units immediately. The final comment claims a one-segment restriction that the function does not implement. This is the exact forbidden E-to-C endpoint shortcut. Progress needs ordered continuity from the previously earned segment plus actual body displacement/support/reference validation, never later-segment proximity. Add a regression that walking the direct six-unit E-to-C shortcut cannot earn the 18-unit comparison and that standing at C/repeated stationary calls cannot advance it. Do not solve only by slowing a scalar toward the projected endpoint: a timer would still grant unwalked progress.
5. `evaluateOfferedSpan` currently uses the same grounded sample for `walkedSegmentSupported` and `checkReference`. Reference targets must be worker sockets at grounded sample +1.85; footing checks need the grounded samples. Passing the feet directly to the fixed socket makes the downward ray enter the connected cap and invalidates even the signed long route. Keep those coordinate meanings separate and qualify the actual exported long/short/common routes against the staged socket/solid geometry. Do not remove cap/backing collisions or change socket heights to make tests pass.

6. `walkedSegmentSupported` currently intersects only the grounded center line against raw AABBs. A feet-level path at y=51.05 can pass under the backing's lo.y=51.35 even though the upright body hits it. This must be an actual body sweep/clearance query against the same literal solids (with the appropriate body height/radius), not just a foot point. Keep fixture/render AABBs unchanged; checking the body's extent is different from enlarging the fixture into a hidden wall. Add a regression for a grounded body crossing under the backing and for a genuinely clear path beside it. The existing player physics alone cannot protect the separately posed worker.

### Follow-up on the 37-test pass

The engineer's own tests have now caught part of item 4, and item 5 now uses `workerSocket(samples[index])`; retain that fix and qualify the actual exported routes. The newer `routeProgressUnits` still uses a default `maxAdvanceUnits=3` and compares `arc` against a `best` value that can advance repeatedly inside the same scan. A stationary body at E with previousUnits=0 can already receive two units from the next segment's proximity. Limit progress by actual observed displacement and ordered continuity, with zero new credit for repeated stationary samples; do not let multiple loop iterations compound an allowance. Keep the valid path test alongside the direct-shortcut and stationary tests.

The malformed-sample state test currently checks `broken?.survey.slot` is null, which accepts a partial graft. The contracted behavior is rejection of the entire inconsistent snapshot; change the behavior and test together, keeping consistent saved earned state resumable.

## Score eligibility when resuming unfinished progress

`beginCommonGroundFinalTexture(beat, hydrated)` must reject a completion restored from storage, while still allowing the first NEW physically earned completion after Continue from an unfinished save. The current snapshot `hydrated` flag describes the entire loaded snapshot, so do not leave it as a permanent ban on all later live anchors/score. Model the live completion edge separately or clear restore-only presentation suppression after revalidation; add a resumed-unfinished-to-fresh-completion case alongside the completed-save/no-replay case. Audio unavailable/muted at that real edge must cancel eligibility rather than queue it for a later unlock.

## Director / actor first wiring check (07:40 UTC)

Please re-read this entire inbox before verification; several initial pure-module findings remain open and now affect callers. These are bounded implementation corrections, not a contract change.

8. Revision still visibly replays the first approach: `commitCommonGroundTailReopen` and `commitCommonGroundSpanOffer` set `workerAtStart=false`; drawing calls `driveInspection`; then `tickWorkerTest` uses W->samples[0] and a new full-path key. `setCommonGroundLeg` resets travelled to zero and immediately samples the path's first point. Preserve the actual last tested pose/prefix through editing and re-offer; create only a suffix leg from that pose. No W teleport, S replay, or full-path re-test on revision. Preserve the equivalent actual safe pose on Continue. Add integration-level regression, since pure slot tests cannot establish actor continuity.
9. Required-world queries currently fail open. In `tickWorkerTest`, missing footing makes all samples supported; `tickCommon` missing footing makes the whole route supported; trace drawing accepts missing ground and only checks the new point, not the actual walked segment/body. No real measurement can succeed until the mounted actual world/ground/solid binding is ready. Suspend safely and earn zero progress while unavailable. Apply actual displacement/segment checks to the Terra comparison too, not only point support.
10. Final reference suspension currently still allows the fixed reference as fallback in `evaluateOfferedSpan`, and H->E positioning ignores far-reference occupancy/LOS. The signed final comparison requires the occupied offered T reference. A vacant/blocked far reference must freeze the actual pose and preserve earned progress, including uncredited repositioning if its reference is required. On reentry, resume from the same pose without another F. `permittedUnits < state.travelled` currently causes `tickCommonGroundActor` to assign target backwards, teleporting to an earlier supported prefix. Never rewind earned position on a transient hold.
11. `commonGroundActorArrived()` allows 0.35 units short of the leg; caller then promotes a fully tested prefix/completion and next leg resets to its start. Final proof requires all 18 actually traversed units and actual final arrival, and positioning must not jump the last fraction of a leg. Clip integration exactly at the endpoint instead of crediting an unwalked remainder. Regression: no commit at 17.65/18 and no >actual-step pose jump across leg changes.
12. Hold/clearance events need physical edges: the full future-span scan currently sets `held`/fires specific-hold immediately even while actor is still walking the supported prefix. Vacancy anchors with `{once:false}` are emitted every tick in the hold branches, and actor-body-clearance holds do not set a truthful survey hold reason. Publish the specific hold when the worker actually reaches its safe stopping point; emit vacancy/resume once per real transition, and retain actionable guidance for actual clearance holds.

13. Optional held-reference offers are currently hard-coded to W in both the interaction resolver and commit. W is one qualified example, not a new exclusive station. The signed design permits a player's actual qualified grounded pose, subject to range/LOS/clearance/occupancy. Keep guidance intelligible, but do not silently narrow the verb to only W or prohibit a proactive valid witness before a refusal. The witness contract and qualification notes already describe this.
14. Durable completion is not yet realized by `enterCommonGroundBeat` / `releaseCommonGroundChapter`: leaving ch13 hides/resets the worker, while the actor is supposed to remain a local Origin tester with accepted route and optional repeat. Fresh/resumed completed-world presence must have one pose authority independent of active chapter, no A4 departure replay, and no completion texture replay. Ensure the intended optional repeat/reset has an actual accessible interaction and retains accepted proof; currently no repeat action appears in the resolver.
15. Home review/return facts are world-scoped at Tidegarden while survey/common facts are world-scoped at Origin. Verify Continue and world switches use those two durable records plus normal milestones consistently; do not require Origin's fresh snapshot to contain Tidegarden-only flags or erase a partially entered chapter because `alreadyEntered` contains fault-reviewed. The schema consistency rule must match real world ownership, not graft both records globally.

## Necessary registry boundary completion

Root has added `StoryDebugPanel.tsx#BEAT_LABELS` and `tidegardenRoute.ts#resolveStoryBootWorldId` to the exact lock/brief under the standing user delegation, with original bytes recovered from HEAD and verified against initial hashes. Keep the narrow changes. `producer-boundary-completion.json` explicitly records the late-reporting deviation; do not claim the older gate covered these paths. Report future missing paths before editing; root can resolve within standing scope. The entire inbox above remains a required pre-verification correction list.

16. Mounted apparatus currently has no physical colliders (`CommonGroundWorld.tsx` only draws instanced meshes/registers chapter query data). Register the same literal AABBs as real player colliders too; the existing HeroAppleTree fixed RigidBody/CuboidCollider is a relevant local precedent. A route guard alone cannot stop the player's live body walking through the visible housing. Ensure world-id readiness gates queries, and keep terrain revision live: `createLiveAgentSurfaceTerrain` itself returns a captured revision string, and `revision: terrain.revision` copies that string; neither value moves when edits occur, despite the component comment. Verify edits are observed and only genuinely invalidated tested support is retired. Record actual render/resource budgets as unmeasured until independent capture; comments declaring two draw calls are not whole-chapter performance evidence.

Root source-preservation scan also found `beats/definitions.ts` changed by the registry generator while still listed protected. Its original bytes were recovered from your initial read and verified against initial hashes. Root has explicitly moved this necessary generated view into the lock/brief allowed boundary for only the four ch13 imports/map entries; old declarations remain protected in meaning. This is recorded as a late generator-output boundary discovery, not backdated approval.

# Common Ground — integration report

One engineer, one chapter. Implemented against the signed `scene-v1` contract
(`ecce3e98…baac3a74`), whose gate receipt and three director signatures were
verified — and whose live bytes were re-hashed — before the first edit.

## Blocking condition found at the end, not caused here

**The frozen contract was replaced in place with an unsigned `scene-v2` while
implementation was under way.** `scene-contract.json` now hashes
`4dbf722b…fddff88e` and declares `contractVersion: scene-v2`, while
`contract-gate-pass.json` and `director-signoffs.json` are both still `scene-v1`.
The producer's own record says so: *"promoted exact scene-v2; three fresh
signatures and contract gate pending."*

I did not move the runtime pins. The AV generator, the registry catalog and the
story-authority identity still name `scene-v1`, so five gate invocations now
fail — and that is them working. They are reporting, correctly, that the bytes
the runtime is bound to are no longer the bytes on disk:

- `chapter:registry:check` — 2 of 4285 (`scene.contract-hash`, `scene.contract-identity`)
- `chapter:registry:smoke`, `scene:av:check` — the same cause
- `story:authority`, `story:authority:smoke` — 1 of 1039 (`production.contract-identity`)

All five passed clean before the re-freeze. Re-pinning them to an unsigned
revision would have been the one thing the whole gate chain exists to prevent,
so the chapter stays bound to the revision three directors actually signed.

Per the inbox, the common-only planned/unverified **guide exception is not
implemented**. When root posts the three-signature gate for `scene-v2`, the
re-pin is mechanical: the sha and revision in `generate-scene-av-runtime.mjs`,
`signedSceneAvRuntime.ts`, `chapter-registry.json` and `story-authority.json`,
a regenerate, and the two changed strings (`guidance/objectives/9` marker label,
`guidance/objectives/13` work order and enter anchor).

## What is actually implemented

Four registered beats, seventeen signed objective rungs, twenty-eight signed
anchors each dispatched from its real physical owner, six moods through the
existing score facade, a walking actor, a persisted world-scoped snapshot, and
a movie bridge that now runs from inside the station all the way into ch13.

**The chapter's own state and geometry** — `commonGroundState.ts`,
`commonGroundRoute.ts`. Pure, no React, no THREE, no clock. Two trace slots
(`accepted` with the class it earned, `working` for the current proposal), real
walked distance carried per sample so wandering between samples is charged
against the 120-unit cap, a tail revision that returns only the discarded tail's
distance and never bumps on a no-op, and strict hydration that rejects the whole
snapshot on any impossible tuple rather than grafting a partial one. References
are socket to socket; the fixed socket is written as the qualified literal
because `51.05 + 1.3` lands six femtometres inside the cap and makes the
instrument occlude itself from everywhere. Walk queries sweep the actual body,
not a foot point, because the backing's underside is above the ground plane.
Progress along a route is bounded by observed displacement and ordered
continuity, so standing at C is worth nothing and the six-unit endpoint
shortcut cannot buy the eighteen-unit passage.

**The runtime** — `commonGroundDirector.ts`, `commonGroundActor.ts`,
`commonGroundScore.ts`, `world/CommonGroundWorld.tsx`, `beats/ch13/`,
`autopilot/rail-ch13-*.ts`. The chapter re-activates from `done` free play at the
actual restored Tidegarden core via `reactivateStoryAtBeat`, and it can tell a
live install from a restored save by watching the receipt appear rather than by
trusting a flag. Every commit is downstream of a physical act, is idempotent,
and is refused from the wrong beat. Every world query fails closed. His refusals
name a literal cause and are published where his body actually stops. A revision
resumes from his real pose — no walk back to W, no replay of the approach — and
a reload resumes his pose, his leg and his walked units rather than giving them
back. The apparatus is a real fixed collider as well as a drawn one.

**The boundary** — the registry gains a named `externalTransitions` record for
`ch10 -> ch13-via-station`, because chapter 10 ends in flight at a station
standoff and chapter 13 begins on foot at a repaired hearth, and two host
segments run between them. Ordinary adjacency is untouched and still exact;
nothing was added to ch10's exit and nothing was dropped from ch13's entry. The
transition's hosts, receipts and evidence are bound to real producers, with ten
negative self-tests covering invented, renumbered and dropped receipts, unknown
hosts, unresolvable evidence, duplicate and non-adjacent pairs, and a transition
declaring a gap that does not exist.

**The movie** — the station screening no longer ends at a shop counter. It holds
on the concourse, then walks out through the interior's own airlock objective and
presses the same [F]. The return URL carries `movie=1` and never `story=`. The
old station bridge yields once departure exists instead of flying back into the
door it came out of, a new return bridge crosses home and presses the shipped
`story-ch12-install-bonded-cell`, and the flight directive now steers for the
post-terminal bridges and for `ch13-return` — which it previously did not do for
any bridge, so their thrust was being asserted into a directive nobody read.

## Commands

`npm run typecheck` pass · `npm run test` 348 files / 2972 tests pass ·
`npm run build` pass · `chapter:journey:check` 0 issues ·
`chapter:journey:smoke`, `guidance:target-check`, `story:ladder:check`,
`preview:check`, `catalog:check`, `creative:workflow:check`, `creative:smoke`
pass · the five contract-pin gates fail for the single external reason above.

`npm run verify`, the visual gate and every headed/GPU probe were deliberately
not run: they belong to the independent story-verifier.

## Honest limitations

No frame, draw, material, program or memory budget is measured — the two-mesh
shape is a design intent, not evidence. No audio was heard. No cold journey,
movie run or screenshot exists. The two preparation work orders under
`ch13:survey:test` and `ch13:common:reciprocal` are engineer-authored
truthfulness copy required by the signed acceptance criteria, published under
the same signed ids and marker labels with one entry acknowledgement each;
scene-v2 appears to formalize exactly this, and adopting its exact strings waits
on its gate. `StoryDebugPanel.tsx` and `tidegardenRoute.ts` were reported as
outside the original boundary before being edited and were then added to it by
root. The story-authority gate's active-production identity is now structural
rather than a frozen literal; the single genuine relaxation is documented in
`integration-report.json#/honestLimitations`.

Nothing was published, deployed, reset, stashed or checked out. The release
ceiling remains `ch4-arrival`.
